classification.difficultyReason: Construct a diagram from the verbal data and connect perpendicular, bisecting diagonals with vertex-angle bisection. Use inverse tangent on a half-diagonal triangle, double its angle, and infer the remaining angles using rhombus properties.

content.prompt: The diagonals of a rhombus have lengths 7 cm and 10 cm. Find the angles of the rhombus correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$69.98^{\circ}$ and $110.02^{\circ}$ (two of each).

Use the perpendicular bisecting diagonals to find a half-angle, then double it.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles and bisect its vertex angles. Their half-lengths are $3.5$ cm and $5$ cm. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the longer diagonal and a side.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{3.5}{5}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.5}{5}\right)\\\theta&\approx34.992020^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The acute vertex angle is
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.5}{5}\right)\\\alpha&\approx69.98^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

Adjacent angles of a rhombus sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^{\circ}-2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.5}{5}\right)\\\beta&\approx110.02^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

Opposite angles are equal, so there are two angles of $69.98^{\circ}$ and two of $110.02^{\circ}$.
